verdict.rationale: Ente's own self-hosting docs explicitly cover running Ente Auth against your own server at `http://<machine-ip>:3003` and pointing the mobile apps at it, and Ente states its server is open source. Together with end-to-end encrypted sync, that is a first-party self-hosted sync path. The pack only has brief snippets, though, so the setup depth and the guarantee that every secret stays inside the perimeter are not shown. missing for 10: detailed server install/operations documentation, explicit evidence of no external dependencies or telemetry to Ente infrastructure, independent hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted Auth deployment.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the sync server on my own infrastructure and keep every secret inside my perimeter

citations.quote: Alternatively, if using Ente Auth, get started by adding an account (assuming you are running Ente Auth at `http://<machine-ip>:3003` or `http://localhost:3003`).
Ente's apps and server are open source
Your codes sync across all your devices, end-to-end encrypted.
